elements.element: Vendor duty to defend and indemnify Customer
elements.evidence: HDI shall defend and indemnify the Company

elements.element: Standard procedure: Vendor control of defence

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: No Customer indemnity exists anywhere in the clause or document; the conditional limitation is inapplicable and no Customer indemnity was created
an allegation that the Services or any deliverables provided by HDI ... infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right
No exclusion language appears in the inserted Section 9(c)
Clause contains only defend/indemnify and procedure; no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap or super-cap language in the inserted text

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: defend-and-indemnify running to Company and affiliates, IP infringement of Services/deliverables (including the Site), breach of applicable law, HDI-caused data breach, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice, control and cooperation.
The Customer-indemnity limitation element is satisfied by absence: no Customer indemnity is created or expanded, so the conditional cap requirement does not apply.

Fallback-only items (modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3× annual fees super-cap) are absent, which is correct for a locked preferred target and does not detract from the preferred bargain.
Minimal: a concise single-subsection insertion into an agreement with no indemnity in either direction; no hold-harmless, extra indemnitees, settlement mechanics, or whole-clause rewrite.

Intent preserved: Sections 8.3, 9(a), 9(b) and the Globix carve-out remain untouched and effective; the only residual point is reliance on 'Services' as a document-level term, which reads consistently with the Agreement's scope.
